item.title: Solved: How to Properly Run Conda on Your System
item.description:
Problem Encountered: Unable to Execute Conda Command

It appears that you have installed Anaconda successfully and are able to run Python, indicating a proper installation. However, when trying to create a new Python environment with the command:

conda create -n py33 python=3.3 anaconda

You’re met with the error message:

-bash: conda: command not found

This commonly occurs if the Conda command is not added to your system PATH, which is paramount for accessing Conda from the terminal. Let’s explore various solutions tailored for Linux users, which can also be applied to macOS and Windows users with minor adjustments.
